title: Stoicism is a Hellenistic school with physics, logic, and ethics
summary: The Stanford entry treats the three parts as one system and notes the thin primary record.
body: Marion Durand, Simon Shogry, and Dirk Baltzly's Stanford Encyclopedia entry introduces Stoicism as a school whose doctrines interlock across physics, logic, and ethics, and it reviews the extant sources. Zeno of Citium is the traditional founder. The v1 article's dates for Zeno, Epictetus, Seneca, and Marcus Aurelius were not copied from this fetch. The four cardinal virtues are older Greek ethics that Stoics used, not a Stoic invention established here. "Dichotomy of control" is a modern label for a point Epictetus does make, in other words, in the Enchiridion.
